To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the notion of an observation can be generalized in order to accommodate the uncertainty of the communication between the considered system and the observer.

(i) uncertain observations can be accommodated in the diagnosis of discrete-event systems; (ii) uncertain observations can provide more information than traditional observations; (iii) uncertain observations are more informative than complex observations; (iv) uncertain observations can lead to a more efficient diagnostic process.

1) uncertain observations are a generalization of traditional observations, and can be exploited by a diagnostic approach for traditional observations, 2) complex observations, which are a generalization both of traditional and uncertain observations, are useful in the diagnosis of active systems, and 3) a sample application of complex observations to a real system, namely power transmission networks, has shown their potential in the diagnosis of such systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diagnosis of systems that are modeled as discrete-event systems and whose observations are uncertain.

the development of a formal framework for diagnosis of uncertain discrete-event systems, with the introduction of a novel notion of uncertain observation and with the accommodation of this notion within a graph-based representation.
the development of a formal framework for the diagnosis of discrete-event systems in the presence of uncertain temporal observations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed framework provides the necessary tools to deal with uncertainty in the observation of discrete-event systems.

the proposed principles and notions can be exploited for a variety of diagnostic approaches and applications, while the proposed techniques are not limited to a single class of systems or to a specific diagnostic approach.
the proposed framework is general and can be used in a variety of diagnostic applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the context of diagnosis of discrete-event systems, we have introduced the notion of an observation that can be underconstrained, and we have shown that this can be exploited to solve several traditional diagnostic problems at once, and thus improve the diagnostic performance of a system.

we have introduced the notion of an observation for discrete event systems, we have introduced a number of principles that affect both the observations and modeled behavior of a discrete-event system and finally we have proposed a new notion of an observation, the uncertain temporal observation and we have introduced the concept of a complex observation.
we have developed a theory of uncertain observations and their use in the context of discrete event systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the notion of an observation is a key concept in the diagnosis of discrete-event systems and that the nature of this concept may vary according to the considered class of systems.
, in the context of discrete-event diagnosis, the observation is not necessarily the only source of uncertainty, as it is often the case for continuous systems.
uncertainty in the observations is a fundamental issue that must be taken into account in the design of any diagnostic system.
